title: Relativistic Algebra over Finite Ring Continuum

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$ with primitive roots; $\gen^{\p-1}=1$; $-1$ is a square in $\Fp$ iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$ (Euler's criterion); the affine maps $x\mapsto a+bx$, $b\neq0$, are the bijections preserving the field structure up to relabelling.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The sign of the quarter-turn exponent: the oriented quarter-turn is $\im=\gen^{-\kap}=-\gen^{\kap}$, the exponent negative by pullback covariance (00:C7); the positive-exponent reading is the conjugate chart. Declared here, derived in the corpus.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The finite subgroups of $SO(3)$: cyclic, dihedral, tetrahedral ($12$), octahedral ($24$), icosahedral ($60$) --- Klein's classification; the binary icosahedral group as the $600$-cell's vertices. Imported for G4.

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The shell, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$ prime; the Subject's frame $(\tau;0,1,\gen)$ with $\gen$ a primitive root and the drive $x\mapsto\gen x$; the cycle $\Phi_\p\cong C_{\p-1}$; $\im:=-\gen^{\kap}$ (A2), $-1=\gen^{2\kap}$.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: Symmetry completeness (Thm.~\ref{thm:symmetric-completeness}): the fourth roots of unity form the unique order-four subgroup $Q_4=\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$; under the Klein four-group $\langle x\mapsto-x,\,x\mapsto x^{-1}\rangle$, $Q_4$ is the union of the two size-two orbits $\{\pm1\}$, $\{\pm\im\}$, and $\Fpx\setminus Q_4$ splits into exactly $\kap-1$ orbits of size four. For $\p\equiv3\pmod4$ no $\im$ exists.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The oriented quarter-turn: $\im=-\gen^{\kap}$ satisfies $\im^{2}=-1$ for every primitive root $\gen$; the two square roots of $-1$ are $\{-\gen^{\kap},\gen^{\kap}\}$, so the drive fixes which is $\im$. On $\F_{13}$, $\gen=2$: $\im=5$.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: Affine reframing (Def.~\ref{def:framed-field}, Lemma~\ref{lem:affine-invariance}): $\varphi_{a,b}(x)=a+bx$, $b\neq0$, is a ring isomorphism $(\Fp,+,\cdot)\to(\Fp,\oplus,\otimes)$ with origin $a$ and unit $a+b$; every polynomial identity is frame-covariant.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Origin and unit are observer data (affine gauge); the generator $\gen$ is the Subject's drive, not gauge; the observer's window is the naturals below $\sqrt\p$ (00:B8).

blocks.title: Arithmetic symmetries and the orbital complex

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The four symmetries as maps of the shell: the successor $C_1:k\mapsto k+1$; translations $T_a$, $a\in\Fp$, the cycle $C_\p$; scalings $S_m$, $m\in\Fpx$, the cycle $C_{\p-1}$; power maps $P_\varepsilon:x\mapsto x^{\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in C_{\p-1}$, bijective iff $\gcd(\varepsilon,\p-1)=1$.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: The frame group (Prop.~\ref{prop:frame-group}): $\langle T_a,S_m\rangle$ is the affine group of order $\p(\p-1)$, acting simply transitively on the frames $(a,b)$, $b\neq0$; the set of frames is a torsor under it (00:C5, 00:D13).

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: Meridians and latitudes (Def.~\ref{def:orbit-sphere}): $M_n(a)=a\gen^{n}$, $a\in\Fp$, the ordered list of the shell with step $\gen^{n}$; $L_a(m)=a\gen^{m}$, $m\in C_{\p-1}$, $a\neq0$, the multiplicative cycle from $a$; the orbital complex $\Sp$ with vertex set $\{(n,\pm a)\}\cup\{0\}$. The $2$-sphere reading is 2-geometry's~\cite{akhtman2025geometry}.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Involutions and counts (Def.~\ref{def:orbit-sphere}\,(a)--(c)): $M_n(a)=M_{n+2\kap}(-a)$ and $L_a(m)=L_{-a}(m+2\kap)$ since $\gen^{2\kap}=-1$; $\p-1$ distinct meridian lists in $2\kap$ great circles; $2\kap$ latitude pairs; one-sided vertex count $(\p-1)^{2}/2+1$, the double cover $(\p-1)^{2}$ (00:B11).

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: Framed integers (Def.~\ref{def:integers}): the window $W_H=\{z\in\Z:|z|\le H\}$, $2H<\p$, embedded by $z\mapsto z\bmod\p$; sign, order and magnitude are the window's; sums read back for $4H<\p$, products for $2H^{2}<\p$ --- the corpus window $\sqrt\p$ (00:B1).

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The window law: $z\mapsto z\bmod\p$ is injective on $W_H$ when $2H<\p$; for $x,y\in W_H$ the residue of $x\pm y$ reads back the integer when $4H<\p$, and that of $xy$ when $2H^{2}<\p$ (the same injectivity on the windows $2H$ and $H^{2}$).

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Framed rationals (Def.~\ref{def:rationals}): $a/b$ with $a,b\in W_H$, $b\not\equiv0$, of value $ab^{-1}\in\Fp$; the scale grid $[x,n]:=x\gen^{-n}$, $x\in\{0,\dots,\p-1\}$, $n\in C_{\p-1}$; $G_n$ the ordered list $(x\gen^{-n})_x$, the meridian $M_{-n}$ of C3.

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: Scale-periodicity (Lemma~\ref{thm:scale-periodicity}, in the field): $S_n(x)=x\gen^{-n}$ satisfies $S_{n+(\p-1)}=S_n$; the grids $G_n$ are $(\p-1)$-periodic as ordered lists; the zoom $[x,n]\mapsto[x,n+1]$ has order $\p-1$. As lists of rationals $x/\gen^{n}$ ($\gen$ lifted to $\Z$) the grids are not periodic: the periodicity is a relation of the field.

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: The continuum as chart (Def.~\ref{def:reals}, Props.~\ref{prop:total-bounded}--\ref{prop:compactness}, Cor.~\ref{cor:knowability}): the framed real line is the reading of the nested grids against $\R$, a labelled idealisation entered nowhere as an object (00:B1); no completion, compactness or ``complete continuum'' is claimed.

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The framed complex chart (Def.~\ref{def:complex}): the pair $(a,b)\in W_H^{2}$ read as $a+b\im\in\Fp$; the quarter-turn acts on the shell as the rotation $x\mapsto\im x$ of order four; the chart is the plane picture of $Q_4$ acting on the shell, not an extension of $\Fp$.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: The extension by $X^{2}+1$ is trivial (Prop.~\ref{prop:Cp-field} reversed): on the shell $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)\cong\Fp\times\Fp$ has zero divisors, $(X+\im)(X-\im)=0$, so it is not a field; $\Fp[X]/(X^{2}+1)$ is a field exactly when $\p\equiv3\pmod4$; the quadratic extension of the shell is $\Fp[\eta]$, $\eta^{2}=\nu$ a non-square (8-dirac B6).

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: No element of additive order two (Thm.~\ref{thm:no-south-pole}): $2s=0$ forces $s=0$; the antipode of the origin on the additive cycle is not a residue; it sits between $2\kap=(\p-1)/2$ and $2\kap+1=(\p+1)/2=2^{-1}$ (20-rh B8).

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: The antipode named $\infty$: the horizon of the observer at $0$ (00:C25, 00:D13), the compactification point of the framed line [chart]; its reading as classical infinity is the chart, not a residue.

rows.label: G1
rows.predicate: Solving in the substrate (first clause): $f\in\Fp[X]$ has a root in $\Fp$ iff $f$ and $X^{\p}-X=\prod_{a}(X-a)$ are not coprime; the gcd counts the distinct roots and Cantor--Zassenhaus splitting finds them, exactly. An equation without a root in $\Fp$ is recognised, not extended (E2).

rows.label: G2
rows.predicate: Limit-like approximation (second clause), across the tower: for every real $r$ and $\varepsilon>0$ some shell $\p=4\kap+1$ carries a framed rational $x/2^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, within $\varepsilon$ of $r$ (primes $\equiv1\pmod4$ beyond every bound). One shell resolves to D5's bound; the limit is the tower, not a completion.

rows.label: G3
rows.predicate: Continuous symmetry, the abelian case (third clause): $\Fpx\simeq C_{\p-1}\simeq SO(2,\Fp)$ (6:E2) is a $\pi/(\p-1)$-net of $U(1)$ under $k\mapsto e^{2\pi\im k/(\p-1)}$; the rounding $k(\theta)=\lfloor(\p-1)\theta/2\pi+\tfrac12\rfloor$ has angle and chord error $\le\pi/(\p-1)$ and group-law defect at most one step.

rows.label: G4
rows.predicate: Continuous symmetry, the non-abelian obstruction: no finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ is an $\varepsilon$-net for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0=\arccos\big((3\sqrt5-1)/8\big)\approx44.5^\circ$, the covering radius of the icosahedral group (A3); the tetrahedral, cyclic and dihedral groups have radius $\ge\pi/2$, the octahedral $\approx62.8^\circ$. Finite subgroups cannot approximate $SO(3)$; the window does (G5).

rows.label: G5
rows.predicate: Continuous symmetry, the non-abelian case resolved by the window: the framed quaternions $W_H^{4}$, read in a shell $\p>8H^{2}$, compose exactly (products land in $W_{4H^{2}}$); normalised, they are an $\varepsilon$-net of $SO(3)$ with $\varepsilon\le2\arcsin(1/H)$ (round $Hs$ to the lattice). At $H=3$, $\p=73$: $38.9^\circ<\varepsilon_0$, finer than any finite subgroup; measured $30.0^\circ$.

rows.label: V1
rows.predicate: The package \texttt{src/1-algebra}, three block scripts, sixteen checks, one notebook: \src{a\_shell}, A1--A5 (orbit census on seven shells with controls, every primitive root, all $428$ frames of $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$, the frame group); \src{b\_numbers}, B1--B6 (window law, grids, the chart of the grid, zero divisors, Thm.~\ref{thm:no-south-pole}, Lemma~\ref{lem:euclid-bound}'s step count); \src{c\_conjecture}, C1--C5 (root test, tower, circle net, covering radii, the window net). Eleven \textsf{EXACT}, five \textsf{CHART}.

rows.label: V2
rows.predicate: \texttt{lean/FrcLedger/Algebra.lean} (\texttt{finite-ring-space}; Lean~4.34, Mathlib 15~Sep~2026; kernel-checked by CI on every push): eighteen theorems --- B3, B4, D4, F1 for every shell, G1 over $\Fp$, G2--G3 over $\R$, complete; B2, C4, D2, E2 with a clause outstanding; B3 on $\F_{13}$; Lemma~\ref{lem:euclid-bound}'s step count by \texttt{decide}. Classical (tier~2): on Mathlib's hierarchy every proof reaches \texttt{Classical.choice}; correct theorems, not the finitist witness (V3).

rows.label: V3
rows.predicate: \texttt{lean/FrcCore} (no Mathlib, \emph{no axioms}: every declaration prints ``does not depend on any axioms''): residues with representatives; the frame $(\chron;0,1,\gen)$, the drive primitive and generating (decidable, by the pigeonhole); the division algorithm from \texttt{Nat.mod}'s definition; polynomials as coefficient sequences; B2, B3, B4, C2, C4, D2, D4, E2, F1, G1's criterion, G5's finitary clause, every shell, by computation and induction.

rows.label: O1
rows.predicate: The conjecture of the conclusion, what remains after G1--G5: the Lie-algebra layer --- one-parameter subgroups and their generators inside the window, where iterating a window rotation $m$ times consumes range as $H^{2m}$; whether the Cayley step of 8-dirac (8:C4) supplies exact one-parameter subgroups of the window net on every shell is open.

B2.name: FRC.Algebra.quarter_turn_exists
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, existence clause): on the shell `card F = 4κ+1` a quarter-turn `u` with `u² = −1` exists. Mathlib: `FiniteField.isSquare_neg_one_iff`.

B2.name: FRC.Algebra.klein_orbit_four
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, orbit clause), 2:D7: for a unit `x` with `x² ≠ 1` and `x² ≠ −1` the four elements `x, −x, x⁻¹, −x⁻¹` of the Klein-four orbit are pairwise distinct (any field of characteristic `≠ 2`); the structural set `{1, i, −1, −i}` is exactly the complement.

B2.name: FRC.Algebra.card_fourth_roots
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the structural set): the fourth roots of unity number exactly `4` on the shell. Mathlib: `IsPrimitiveRoot.card_rootsOfUnity`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quarter_turn_exists
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, existence clause) — a quarter-turn `u` with `u² = −1` exists on every shell.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.fourth_roots
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the structural set) — the fourth roots of unity are exactly `1, −1, i, −i`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.klein_orbit_four
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1 of 1-algebra), 2:D7 — off the fourth roots of unity, `x`, `−x`, `x⁻¹`, `−x⁻¹` are four distinct residues (`y` stands for the inverse: `x·y = 1`).

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_rep
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the count, existence), 2:D7 — every residue off `Q₄` lies in the Klein orbit of some `g^r` with `1 ≤ r < κ`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_rep_unique
B2.doc: 1:B2 (Theorem 1, the count, uniqueness), 2:D7 — two representatives `g^r`, `g^{r'}` with `1 ≤ r, r' < κ` whose orbits meet are the same: the Klein orbits off `Q₄` are exactly `κ − 1`, one for each `r ∈ [1, κ)`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.s13_klein
B2.doc: 1:B2 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the fourth roots of unity are `{1, 5, 12, 8}`, and every other nonzero residue has four distinct companions `{x, −x, x⁻¹, −x⁻¹}`: the two Klein orbits `{2, 11, 7, 6}` and `{3, 10, 9, 4}`.

B3.name: FRC.Algebra.quarter_turn
B3.doc: 1:B3 (convention 4, the oriented quarter-turn): `i := −g^κ` satisfies `i² = −1`; and `g^(2κ) = −1`, the involution behind Definition 5. From `FrcLedger.Fourier`.

B4.name: FRC.Algebra.affine_frame
B4.doc: 1:B4 (Definition 2, Lemma 1): in the affine frame `(a, b)`, `φ x = a + b x` carries `+` and `·` to `⊕` and `⊗`, is a bijection, and the multiplicative unit of the relabelled field is `a + b`; `b` is the unit only when `a = 0`.

B4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.affine_frame_unit
B4.doc: 1:B4 (Definition 2 of 1-algebra) — in the affine frame `(a, b)` the multiplicative unit is `a + b`, not `b`: `(a + b) ⊗ z = z` for every `z`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Affine.simply_transitive
C2.doc: 1:C2, 4:C5 (the frame group), simple transitivity — for frames `(a, b)` and `(c, d)` (`b, d ≠ 0`) there is exactly one affine map carrying the first to the second: `φ (a, b) := (φ.apply a, φ.b · b)`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frame_count
C2.doc: 1:C2, 4:C5, the order — the frames `(a, b)`, `b ≠ 0`, number `p·(p − 1)`: `p` choices of the origin, `p − 1` of the unit.

D2.name: FRC.Algebra.framed_integer_window
D2.doc: 1:D2 (Definition 6 made precise): the framed-integer window. Integers of absolute value `≤ H` with `2H < card F` have distinct residues: the cast `ℤ → ZMod p` is injective on the window. Stated on `ZMod p`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_injective
D2.doc: 1:D2 (the window law, injectivity) — two window integers `x, y ≤ H` with `2H < p` that read as the same residue are equal: `ofNat x = ofNat y → x = y`. (Both are below `p`, so the residues are the integers.)

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_signed
D2.doc: 1:D2, the signed window: `x` and `−y` (`x, y ≤ H`, `2H < p`) read as the same residue only when both are zero — the window's positive and negative halves do not overlap.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_add_readback
D2.doc: 1:D2, the read-back of sums: for `x, y ≤ H` and `4H < p`, the residue of `x + y` determines the integer `x + y` among the integers `z ≤ 2H`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.window_mul_readback
D2.doc: 1:D2, the read-back of products: for `x, y ≤ H` and `2H² < p`, the residue of `x·y` determines the integer `x·y` among the integers `z ≤ H²`.

D4.name: FRC.Algebra.scale_periodic
D4.doc: 1:D4 (Lemma 2 restated in the field — scale-periodicity): the scale map `S n x = x · g^(−n)` on the shell is `(card F − 1)`-periodic in `n`: the residue grids `G_n = S_n(0..p−1)` coincide as ordered lists.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.scale_periodic
D4.doc: 1:D4 (Lemma 2 of 1-algebra, scale periodicity) — the residue grid repeats with the period `p − 1` of the drive: `g^{n + (p−1)} = g^n`, hence `x·g^{n + (p−1)} = x·g^n` for every `x`.

E2.name: FRC.Algebra.complex_chart_zero_divisor
E2.doc: 1:E2 (Proposition 5 reversed): adjoining a root of `X² + 1` to a field that already contains one gives zero divisors — `F[X]/(X²+1)` is not a field on the shell. With `u² = −1`, `(X + u)(X − u) = 0` in the quotient while both factors are nonzero.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.complex_chart_zero_divisor
E2.doc: 1:E2 (Proposition 5 reversed) — on a shell that already has a square root of `−1` the complex chart is not a field: `(i, 1)·(−i, 1) = (0, 0)` with both factors nonzero (`X + i` and `X − i` are zero divisors).

F1.name: FRC.Algebra.no_south_pole
F1.doc: 1:F1 (Theorem 3): `2s = 0 ⇒ s = 0` in a field of characteristic `≠ 2`: the additive cycle has no element of order two; the antipode of the origin is not a residue.

F1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.no_south_pole
F1.doc: 1:F1 (Theorem 3) — `2s = 0 ⇒ s = 0`: the additive cycle has no element of order two; the antipode of the origin is not a residue.

G1.name: FRC.Algebra.root_iff_not_coprime
G1.doc: 1:G1 (the conjecture's first clause, solving): `f ∈ F_p[X]` has a root in `F_p` iff `f` and `X^p − X = ∏_a (X − a)` are not coprime — the root test is a gcd, exact in the substrate.

G1.name: FRC.Shell.Poly.Frame.root_iff_common_factor
G1.doc: 1:G1, the root criterion — `f` has a root in the shell iff `f` and `X^p − X` share a factor of positive degree. Forward: the factor is `X − a` (synthetic division, Fermat). Backward: a common factor `d` of degree `m ≥ 1` with no root would force its cofactor in `X^p − X`, of degree `p − m < p`, to vanish at all `p` residues, hence to be zero (`root_bound`), against `X^p − X ≠ 0`; the root of `d` is found by deciding `∃ i < p, d(i) = 0`.

G1.name: FRC.Shell.Poly.Frame.root_bound
G1.doc: 1:G1, the root bound — a polynomial of degree at most `n` that vanishes at `n + 1` distinct points is zero: the distinct roots are counted by the degree.

G1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.fermat
G1.doc: 1:G1, the finitary core (Fermat): every residue satisfies `x^p = x` — the polynomial `X^p − X` vanishes on the whole shell, which is what the root test of 1:G1 rests on.

G2.name: FRC.Algebra.tower_density
G2.doc: 1:G2 (second clause, limit-like approximation): the tower of shells resolves every real — for every `r` and `ε > 0` some shell `p = 4κ + 1` carries a framed rational `x / 2^n`, `|x| ≤ 2κ`, within `ε` of `r` (Dirichlet for primes `≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `Nat.exists_prime_gt_modEq_one`).

G3.name: FRC.Algebra.circle_net
G3.doc: 1:G3 (third clause, the abelian case): the rounding `k(θ) = round(Nθ/2π)` puts `2πk/N` within `π/N` of `θ` — `C_N ≅ F_p^×` (`N = p − 1`) is a `π/N`-net of `U(1)`.

G3.name: FRC.Algebra.group_law_defect
G3.doc: 1:G3 (third clause): the group-law defect of the rounding is at most one step.

G5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.quaternion_window
G5.doc: 1:G5, the finitary clause — framed quaternions with window coordinates `≤ H`, read in a shell `p > 8H²`, compose exactly: the product of the readings is the reading of the integer product; that product's coordinates lie in the window `4H²`; and the reading determines it among the window's quaternions.

G5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.read_mul
G5.doc: 1:G5, exact composition — the reading of the integer product is the product of the readings.

V3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.half_period
V3.doc: 2:D1, 00:C1 — the half-period: `g^{2κ} = −1` for the drive of every frame.

V3.name: FRC.Shell.Poly.Frame.root_iff_common_factor
V3.doc: 1:G1, the root criterion — `f` has a root in the shell iff `f` and `X^p − X` share a factor of positive degree. Forward: the factor is `X − a` (synthetic division, Fermat). Backward: a common factor `d` of degree `m ≥ 1` with no root would force its cofactor in `X^p − X`, of degree `p − m < p`, to vanish at all `p` residues, hence to be zero (`root_bound`), against `X^p − X ≠ 0`; the root of `d` is found by deciding `∃ i < p, d(i) = 0`.
